name: Washington
source: Washington levies no tax on wages or retirement income in 2026; second source Tax Foundation, State Individual Income Tax Rates and Brackets 2026 (https://taxfoundation.org/data/all/state/state-income-tax-rates-2026/). Not modelled (the schema has no gains-only tax and no future start year for state brackets): the capital gains excise tax of 7% on long-term gains above a standard deduction (270,000 in 2024, indexed) and 9.9% on gains above 1,000,000 from 2025 (dor.wa.gov news release on 2024 collections, SB 5813); and the 9.9% tax on income above 1,000,000 enacted by SB 6346 (signed 2026-03-30), starting January 1, 2028 and facing a court challenge (Morgan Lewis, KUOW and Washington State Standard, March 2026)

state_base.note: Washington has no state income tax.

estate_inheritance.note: Washington estate tax (RCW 83.100): the brackets tax the Washington taxable estate above the applicable exclusion amount. For deaths on or after July 1, 2026 ESB 6347 returns the rates to the pre-2025 Table W (10% to 20%; base 1,490,000 at 9,000,000) and sets the exclusion at 3,000,000, adjusted yearly by the Seattle-Tacoma-Bremerton CPI. Read on the Department of Revenue estate tax tables page on 2026-10-22 (it lists 3,000,000 for 2027 and after); second source: House bill report on ESB 6347 (lawfilesext.leg.wa.gov) and Mercer Advisors. Deaths from July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026 used 10% to 35% with a 3,076,000 exclusion (2026); not modelled since the model's estate falls after mid-2026. The whole section is marked indexed, so the bracket thresholds grow with inflation too (only the exclusion does by law). No inheritance tax. Not modelled: the farm and family-business deductions and portability (Washington has none, so a couple gets one exclusion).

social_security.note: Washington has no personal income tax, so Social Security benefits are not taxed. Confirmed primary on https://dor.wa.gov/taxes-rates/income-tax (validation run 2, 2026-10-22).

local_income_tax.note: Washington counties and cities levy no income tax (state-costs.csv local_income_tax 'none'; no agency page read). Confirmed primary on https://app.leg.wa.gov/RCW/default.aspx?cite=36.65.030 (validation run 2, 2026-10-22).

sales_tax.check_at: Washington revenue department sales and use tax rate tables
sales_tax.source: Tax Foundation, State and Local Sales Tax Rates, Midyear 2026 (https://taxfoundation.org/data/all/state/2026-sales-tax-rates-midyear/), as of 2026-07-01; groceries and clothing: https://zamp.com/resources/sales-tax-on-groceries and https://zamp.com/blog/sales-tax-on-clothing
sales_tax.note: Rates as fractions; avg_local_rate is the combined less the state rate, at least 0. vehicle_rate is the purchase tax on a car: assumed equal to the combined rate. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py. Groceries and clothing: grocery_rate is the state rate on groceries (0.0) plus the average local rate where locals tax them (locals: no); research note: Food exempt from state and local. clothing_taxable is true (research: yes; taxed). Set by hand from .claude/state/research/grocery-tax.csv and clothing-tax.csv (s329).

property_tax.check_at: Census ACS 2024 1-year tables B25090 and B25082 at https://data.census.gov
property_tax.source: Census ACS 2024 1-year (B25090 / B25082) as compiled at https://floridaprobateandfamilylaw.com/blog/effective-property-tax-rates-by-state-2025/
property_tax.note: Effective rate: real-estate taxes paid divided by home value, owner-occupied homes. Senior relief, homestead caps and freezes are not in it (a buyer pays the full rate). Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

home_insurance.source: Insurify state table for a 300,000 dwelling (https://insurify.com/homeowners-insurance/states/), October 2026
home_insurance.note: Average annual premium for a 300,000 dwelling. Quote averages differ by 20 to 40 percent between publishers, so the model uses it as a ratio between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

car_insurance.source: Insurify full coverage, monthly times 12 (https://insurify.com/car-insurance/states/), October 2026
car_insurance.note: Average annual full-coverage premium. Used as a ratio between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

car_taxes.check_at: https://dol.wa.gov (vehicle tab fees and the RTA excise tax estimator)
car_taxes.source: dol.wa.gov tab fee page (basic fee 43.25; RTA excise 1.1% of depreciated MSRP in the Sound Transit district) and the 2019 House bill report on I-976 (weight fee 25 to 72, other fees about 9)
car_taxes.note: Washington: basic fee 43.25, weight fee 35 to 65 for a typical car (35 at 4,000 lb, 65 at 6,000 lb, for registrations from 2026-01-01; RCW 46.17.365, https://app.leg.wa.gov/RCW/default.aspx?cite=46.17.365, validation run 3, 2026-10-22) and filing fees of about 15 (about 110 a year), plus the RTA excise of 1.1% of depreciated value in the Sound Transit district (about 270 on a car worth 25,000 there, about 130 averaged over the state's population); about 240 in all. A rough estimate. Typical car, averaged over about ten years of ownership; registration and vehicle taxes only (no title, plate or inspection fees). Set by hand after the import: rerunning importStateCosts.py resets it to 0. Accepted: low impact (triage 2026-10-23): Built from statute pieces.

fuel.source: Excise: https://dol.wa.gov/vehicles-and-boats/prorate-and-fuel-tax/news-updates (validation run 2, 2026-10-22); price: USGasGauge state-by-year table (AAA data), 2024 annual average
fuel.note: gas_tax_per_gallon is the state excise in dollars, without sales tax on fuel: 0.565 from 2026-07-01 (0.554 before); average_price_per_gallon is the 2024 average pump price (grade unclear, about regular). Price confirmed primary on https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=PET&s=EMM_EPMR_PTE_SWA_DPG&f=A (validation run 3, 2026-10-22). Set by hand from the primary source in validation run 2, 2026-10-22; importStateCosts.py keeps a hand-set section.

utilities.source: EIA Electric Power Monthly Table 5.6.B, residential price, January to July 2026
utilities.note: Average residential electricity price in dollars per kWh, January to July 2026 (a partial year). Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

housing.check_at: https://fred.stlouisfed.org (Zillow Home Value Index by state) and https://meric.mo.gov/data/cost-living-data-series
housing.source: Zillow Home Value Index by state via FRED (September 2026); MERIC Cost of Living Data Series housing index (C2ER, US = 100), Q2 2026
housing.note: typical_home_value is the Zillow Home Value Index (all homes, middle tier); cost_index is the MERIC housing cost index (US = 100), used to scale rent after a move. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

health_premiums.check_at: https://www.kff.org/affordable-care-act/state-indicator/average-marketplace-premiums-by-metal-tier/, Washington insurance department Medigap rate guide and the CMS MA Landscape and Part D files (https://www.cms.gov)
health_premiums.source: KFF Average Marketplace Premiums by Metal Tier 2026 (benchmark silver at 40, times the federal age curve 2.124 for 60); MoneyGeek Medicare Supplement Plan G at 65, 2026; KFF Average Monthly Premium for PDPs, 2024; MedicareSupplement.com analysis of the CMS 2026 MA Landscape files
health_premiums.note: Monthly premiums per person, unsubsidized list prices: aca_60_monthly is the benchmark silver plan at 60 (estimated from the age-40 figure), medigap_g_monthly Plan G at 65, part_d_monthly the enrollment-weighted Part D plan, medicare_advantage_monthly the average Medicare Advantage premium. Null means no usable figure; a move then leaves that premium unchanged. Used as ratios between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv and state-costs-2.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

price_indexes.source: MERIC Cost of Living Data Series grocery index (C2ER, US = 100), Q2 2026; BEA Regional Price Parities by state, goods and other services (US = 100), 2024, release of 2026-02-19 via FRED
price_indexes.note: Price levels with US = 100: grocery_index is the MERIC grocery index, bea_goods and bea_services the BEA Regional Price Parities for goods and for services other than rent. Used as ratios between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv and state-costs-2.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

long_term_care.source: Genworth / CareScout Cost of Care Survey 2024, Ranked State Data Tables, state medians (https://assets.carescout.com/a41bb6478c/298701.pdf)
long_term_care.note: State median monthly costs: a home health aide, an assisted living facility and a private nursing home room. Stored for reference; the model does not use them. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv and state-costs-2.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.
